title: Looking Beyond the Scale: Do Surgical Skill Models Learn Transferable Representations Across Assessment Rubrics?
abstract: arXiv:2608.17519v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Vision-based surgical skill assessment has shown strong in-domain results, yet a fundamental question remains unasked: do these models learn transferable representations of surgical proficiency, or do they merely encode dataset-specific visual patterns?   This paper systematically analyzes what limits cross-domain skill transfer between the GOALS and OSATS assessment scales using the LASANA and JIGSAWS datasets. Each evaluated method serves a targeted diagnostic purpose: end-to-end training to test whether supervised skill learning transfers directly, Adaptive Sharpness-Aware Minimization (ASAM) to probe whether flatter loss landscapes improve generalization, and augmentation-based self-supervised and contrastive learning to assess whether domain-invariant pretraining decouples skill from visual context. Transfer is evaluated in both directions using a disjoint-participant held-out test set for JIGSAWS.   Results reveal an asymmetry: b

translated_title: 超越表面指标：手术技能模型能否在不同评估标准间学习可迁移的表征？
translated_abstract: 基于视觉的手术技能评估在领域内表现出强劲的结果，但一个根本性问题仍未提出：这些模型是真正学习了手术熟练度的可迁移表征，还是仅仅编码了数据集特定的视觉模式？本文使用LASANA和JIGSAWS数据集，系统分析了GOALS和OSATS评估标准之间跨领域技能迁移的局限性。每种评估方法都服务于特定的诊断目的：端到端训练用于测试监督技能学习是否直接迁移；自适应锐度感知最小化（ASAM）用于探究更平坦的损失景观是否能改善泛化；基于增强的自监督和对比学习用于评估领域不变的预训练是否能将技能与视觉情境解耦。迁移在两个方向上进行评估，并使用JIGSAWS的参与者不重叠的留出测试集。结果显示一种不对称性：b
tldr: 本文系统揭示了手术技能模型在GOALS与OSATS评估标准间迁移存在不对称性，表明模型可能仅编码数据集特定的视觉模式，而非通用技能表征。
en_tdlr: This paper systematically reveals an asymmetry in cross-domain transfer of surgical skill models between GOALS and OSATS rubrics, suggesting models may encode dataset-specific visual patterns rather than generalizable skill representations.
